### Model stg_orders
File: models/staging/stg_orders.sql · materialized as view
Description: Cleaned orders, one row per order. Expected volume is 500-1,000 orders over the 180-day window.
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description · tests):
- order_id · INTEGER · Primary key of the order. · tests: unique, not_null
- customer_id · INTEGER · Customer who placed the order (foreign key to stg_customers). · tests: not_null
- order_date · DATE · Date the order was placed. · tests: not_null
- status · VARCHAR · Order lifecycle status. · tests: accepted_values(values=['placed', 'shipped', 'completed', 'cancelled'])
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the row was loaded into the warehouse.
Model-level tests: row_count_between(min_rows=500, max_rows=1000)
SQL (models/staging/stg_orders.sql):
```sql
with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        cast(order_date as date) as order_date,
        status,
        loaded_at
    from source

)

select * from renamed
```

historical_context:
Recent changes (newest first):
- 2026-10-10 · ticket · SHOP-219: web shop store locale switched from en-US to en-ZA (currency display and date formats).
- 2026-10-05 · deploy · Warehouse database file moved to faster storage; no schema changes
- 2026-10-01 · commit d3c24ce · stg_customers: lower-case email and upper-case country code (models/staging/stg_customers.sql)
Previous incidents:
- INC-0351 (2026-08-04): order_date was null for 12 orders after a shop export timeout. Resolution: export re-run, no code change.
Recent run history:
- stg_orders tests, last 7 daily runs: all pass ×6; today (2026-10-13) the test that reads order_date errors.
- New orders per day: 2–5 (normal) for the last 7 days.

gold_standard_remediation.root_cause: From 2026-10-10 the shop writes order_date as DD/MM/YYYY (e.g. '13/10/2026') instead of ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' (e.g. '2026-04-17'), after the SHOP-219 locale change. Because the column now mixes formats, raw_orders.order_date loads as VARCHAR and `cast(order_date as date)` in stg_orders raises a Conversion Error on the 10 new rows. Tests that read order_date error, and the marts are skipped.
gold_standard_remediation.fix: Root fix: ask the shop team to restore ISO 8601 dates in the export (or set the export date format explicitly). Make staging robust in models/staging/stg_orders.sql: `coalesce(try_strptime(cast(order_date as varchar), '%Y-%m-%d'), try_strptime(cast(order_date as varchar), '%d/%m/%Y'))::date as order_date`. Keep the not_null test on stg_orders.order_date so any value matching neither format still fails.
gold_standard_remediation.verification: `dbt build --select stg_orders+` passes. `select count(*) from stg_orders where order_date is null` returns 0 and `select max(order_date) from stg_orders` is today's date, which shows the new rows were parsed and not dropped.
gold_standard_remediation.notes: Do not read the new values as MM/DD: dates such as 05/10 are ambiguous, so the format must be stated explicitly.
gold_standard_remediation.text:
Root cause: From 2026-10-10 the shop writes order_date as DD/MM/YYYY (e.g. '13/10/2026') instead of ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' (e.g. '2026-04-17'), after the SHOP-219 locale change. Because the column now mixes formats, raw_orders.order_date loads as VARCHAR and `cast(order_date as date)` in stg_orders raises a Conversion Error on the 10 new rows. Tests that read order_date error, and the marts are skipped.

Fix: Root fix: ask the shop team to restore ISO 8601 dates in the export (or set the export date format explicitly). Make staging robust in models/staging/stg_orders.sql: `coalesce(try_strptime(cast(order_date as varchar), '%Y-%m-%d'), try_strptime(cast(order_date as varchar), '%d/%m/%Y'))::date as order_date`. Keep the not_null test on stg_orders.order_date so any value matching neither format still fails.

Verification: `dbt build --select stg_orders+` passes. `select count(*) from stg_orders where order_date is null` returns 0 and `select max(order_date) from stg_orders` is today's date, which shows the new rows were parsed and not dropped.

Notes: Do not read the new values as MM/DD: dates such as 05/10 are ambiguous, so the format must be stated explicitly.
